branch: D — A dump ALL ZERO on ALL ranks
interpretation: The BF16 HC weights are NOT present at the subbuffer addresses the contraction binds. The down and up contractions read zero pages: lo = W_down·normalized = 0, and mixed = fold over up(silu(lo)) — with W_up also zero and lo zero, mixed is zero. The subbuffers exist (size 6553600 = 3.27M BF16 elements, plausible for W shards), are distinct per rank (different VkBuffer handles and offsets), but their CONTENT at dispatch time is all-zero.
refined_root_cause: TP5 weight distribution/mirroring chain: BF16 HC weights (down/up) are never uploaded (or are uploaded to a different location than where the A binding points) on ANY of the 5 ranks. The SPIR-V execution layer is exonerated — the kernels faithfully multiply zero weights. This also explains why FORCE_ITER (V-A) changed nothing: both decode paths read the same all-zero weights. And it explains why HC-Q8 (3c) worked: Q8_0 weights go through a different upload path that works.
key_subbuffer_evidence: r0: W_down {buf=0x6419d207ea30, off=1049041280, size=6553600}, W_up {buf=same, off=1055594880} — offsets ~1GB apart in a shared weight buffer, sizes plausible; r1: different buffer handle — per-rank sharding is structurally present, only the CONTENT is zero.
next_candidate_for_engineer: the TP5 tensor-split weight upload path for BF16 HC tensors: where ggml splits W_down/W_up across ranks (--split-mode tensor) and uploads shards; likely the upload is skipped, targets a stale buffer, or the binding offset does not match the upload offset for BF16 (Q8_0 path works).
